name: Blackpill
lead: The blackpill is a fatalistic worldview that originated on incel forums as a more nihilistic version of the manosphere's 'red pill'. It holds that dating and social outcomes are largely determined by physical attractiveness and genetics, and that men seen as unattractive cannot meaningfully change their position.[1]

Its relationship with looksmaxxing is contested within communities: some members say blackpill ideas are the premise that motivates improving looks, while others argue they lead people to give up.[2][3] Researchers have studied incel communities, finding high rates of depression, isolation and suicidality, and some studies on endorsement of violence.[1][4][5]
infobox: Looks and genetics largely determine dating success

paras: Wikipedia reports that the blackpill claims dating success is set by genetics, that women prefer high-status men (hypergamy), and that self-improvement, including looksmaxxing, cannot help unattractive men.[1] According to the Anti-Defamation League, as cited there, followers see options such as giving up ('lie down and rot'), suicide or violence.[1]
By contrast, the red pill emphasizes personal agency, such as improving skills or appearance.[1]

On looksmax.org, users disagree about the blackpill. One thread argues that the blackpill is taking away from what looksmaxxing was meant to be, a way to improve oneself, while saying 'the BP is real' and urging members to work on what they can control.[2] Another thread title calls the blackpill coping by insecure incels, and a poster there argues outdoor interaction and exercise matter more than looksmaxxing products.[3]

Critics cited by Wikipedia call the claims pseudoscientific and say proponents rely on uncritical readings of evolutionary studies; the Institute for Strategic Dialogue calls this 'argument by exhaustion'.[1] The Global Internet Forum to Counter Terrorism says incel beliefs show hallmarks of an extremist ideology.[1]

A study of men in online incel communities found stronger identity fusion with their group than men in other male-dominated groups, and that feeling verified by other incels predicted fusion, which in turn related to endorsing violence against women.[4]

Researchers also report that most surveyed self-identified incels reject violence, and that Costello and Buss argue extreme inceldom resembles suicidality more than violence toward others.[1] A 2025 analysis of 100 psychotherapy threads on an incel forum examined community attitudes toward therapy.[5]
No studies found testing the blackpill as an intervention. Observational research on incel communities is described above.[4][5]

timeline.event: The Matrix popularizes the pill metaphor later adopted by online communities.[6]

lore.intro: Blackpill discussion on looksmax.org ranges from endorsement to rejection, and members debate whether it motivates or discourages self-improvement.[2][3]

claims.claim: Looks largely determine dating and social outcomes.
claims.believers: Proponents describe attractiveness as the main driver of outcomes and say 'the BP is real'.[2]

claims.experts: Researchers describe the blackpill as fatalistic, and incel communities show high rates of depression and suicidality.[1][5]

claims.claim: The blackpill is coping by insecure men.

claims.experts: No published studies were found testing this claim directly.

card.summary: Fatalistic incel-born framework holding that looks and genetics set outcomes; debated inside looksmaxxing.
card.note: Researchers link incel blackpill communities to hopelessness and, for some, extremist views.

quick.overview:
The blackpill is a worldview from incel forums that says physical attractiveness and genetics largely determine dating and social outcomes, and that unattractive men cannot escape their position.

Looksmaxxing members disagree about it: some treat it as a premise for improving looks, others as a trap.
quick.mechanism: It is a belief framework, not a practice; members trade arguments, statistics and personal accounts about looks and status.
quick.risks: Researchers report high rates of depression, isolation and suicidality in incel communities, and some studies link blackpill identification to endorsing violence, though most surveyed incels reject violence.
